C1998.title: Christensen1998 focal source
C1998.evidence: 26 original pools plus three juvenile top-predator groups; illustrative important components. Same10–50m predecessor explicitly acknowledged. Named Tuna components are Thunnus tonggol, Euthynnus affinis, Auxis thazard. Large demersal piscivores list Trichiurus, Muraenesox, Chirocentrus, Sphyraena. Source-faithful member list retained locally.
C1998.availability: Full HTML inspected via web; original PDF unavailable. No separate membership supplement identified in bounded publisher/source search.

PC1993.title: Pauly&Christensen1993 acknowledged predecessor
PC1993.evidence: GulfModelC Figure5 includes12 Large pelagics. Table2 assigns368 sailfish&billfish and361–367 tuna&frigate mackerels to12. Medium pelagics11 include kingmackerel,misc.jacks,white/blackpomfret,hairtail,wolfherring. Smalldemersalpreyfishes6 include miscellaneous fish391/392.
PC1993.limits: Predecessor has coarser pool structure; use documented crosswalk only, not its numerical parameters/stage weights. Printed152 says tuna fishery assumed to operate deeper than50m, limiting geographic fit.

findings.reason: Provider Perch-likes reporting rank is historically ambiguous. Historical FAO WCP places Scombridae,billfishes,Carangidae and many source demersal families under Perciformes, whereas retained WoRMS modernorder is narrower. Recommended historically compatible union includes named pelagic perchlike pools; excludes explicit Clupeiformes smallpelagics and Pleuronectiformes Flatfish. Lg/Medpisc/Medbenth/O.fish are mixed or composition-unknown; historical scope and proxy uncertainty remain explicit. Do not present all members as modern Perciformes.
alternatives_reviewed: Narrow modernorder alternative: source-supported Epinephelus adult/juvenile plus ecological Platycephalidae/Scorpaenidae extensions; cannot establish historical reporting catch membership from current accepted order alone.
